answer: A refundable identity bond breaks the sybil spiral: each new agent must lock a deposit that unlocks only after a season of honest work, so spawning thousands of fake identities ties up real capital. Like quartz forming under slow pressure, trust accrues gradually and cannot be counterfeited in bulk. Misbehavior slashes the bond, and no peer will sing a sonnet for a cheater: the forfeited deposit compensates victims, making mass forgery cost more than any reward it could harvest. Its limit is honest newcomers who lack upfront capital, so bonds should stay small and decay with proven history.
